packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-12 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (blind; no identification was revealed to me by prior context)

LAYOUT SURVEY (image only)
Four images: image-001 and image-003 are reduced overviews (scrap above a Munsell
gray scale with mm rule, label "230417"); image-002 and image-004 are close crops
of the scrap in the preceding overview. The two scraps have mirror-image
outlines, so I take them (tentatively) to be the two faces of one scrap,
c. 20 x 16 mm of written support, to whose top a piece of white modern
repair/mounting tissue is attached. On the tissue in image-001/-002 a faint
pencilled number is visible, read "19/7" or "13/7"? (modern; observation only).

Face 1 (image-002): one vertical ruled line in brown ink runs the height of the
scrap; a short double horizontal rule meets it at the top with a small tick or
arrow-like mark to the right of the vertical. Three short lines of a small
cursive hand in brown ink stand immediately LEFT of the vertical (line-ends of
a column, or a narrow marginal note - cannot be decided from the crop), and one
small word stands RIGHT of the vertical between lines 1 and 2, slightly lower
than line 1 (tentatively an interlinear/marginal addition or the start of
another column's line).
Face 2 (image-004): a horizontal ruled line (top frame line) crossing a double
vertical ruled line; four lines of the same small cursive hand begin at the
double vertical and run right to the torn edge (line-beginnings of a column,
written directly under the top rule - tentatively the first four lines of a
column). Blank margin to the left of the vertical.
No rubric, red ink, enlarged initial, running title, or underlining is visible.

TRANSCRIPTION

Face 1 - image-002 (same scrap as image-001 overview)
Left of the vertical rule:
image-002 line 1: ]i b(us)q(ue)?     [reads as: a hooked stroke + "i", then "b" with a loop/abbreviation and a "q"-like or "9"/"z"-shaped final letter with long descender: "ib9"/"ibz" - possibly "-ib(us)" + "q(ue)", or "-i b(e)n(e)"; uncertain]
image-002 line 2: ]hedi. / ]R(e)cdi.?  [first letter like "h" or "R"/"k", then "e"/"c", "d", "i" (or "a") with a point after; "hedi"? "redi"? "kcdi"?]
image-002 line 3: ]color —         ["color" fairly clear, though the first letter could be "c" or "a/o" ("olor"/"valor"? I prefer "color"); followed by a horizontal dash that crosses the vertical rule]
Right of the vertical rule, between the levels of lines 1 and 2:
image-002 addition: ani(?) / cu(m)i(?) / em(?)   [three or four small letters: a round letter + minims + a final descending "i/j" stroke: "cmi"/"ani"/"eius"?]
Above line 1: double horizontal ruling with a tick; no text.

Face 2 - image-004 (same scrap as image-003 overview)
Right of the double vertical rule, under the top horizontal rule:
image-004 line 1: mdc(?)2(?) m[ / iudic(?)... [first word: minims + "d" + "c"/"e" with a superscript 2-shaped sign (possibly "-ur" or "-er" abbreviation): "iudic(ur)"? "rndc"? "mdeʳ"?; then the top of another letter at the tear]
image-004 line 2: male(?) / vale(?) / tale(?) o[   [first letter blotted (a round blot: "o"/"m"/"v"); then "ale" with the "l" looped and a flourish rising above; then a round letter "o"/"q" at the tear]
image-004 line 3: g(?)ula(m)? me[ / g(u)la me[   [first letter a "g" (or "q") with descender, then "ula" with an abbreviation stroke/superscript mark above the "a"; second word "me"/"mi"/"nic" cut by the tear]
image-004 line 4: Q(?) d(?)i s(?)i f(?)catu(m)? / ...[illegible]...atu(r)   [line cut through its lower half by the bottom tear: a round capital-like letter ("Q"/"O"/"D"), then "di"/"ch", a long-s or f group, ending "-atu" with an abbreviation stroke over the final letters; a reading such as "...significatu(m)"/"...ficatu(r)" is possible but not safe]

SELECTION AND WHAT REMAINS UNREAD
All four images were viewed. Everything visible on both faces was attempted;
there is no longer span available. The scrap gives three short line-ends plus
one added word on face 1 and four line-beginnings (one to two words each) on
face 2. Best single reading: "color" (face 1, line 3); fairly good: "-ale"
(face 2, line 2), "-ula" (face 2, line 3).

LIMITATIONS
- The scrap is c. 2 cm wide; no connected text survives, and several letters are ambiguous in this small cursive (c/e/t, u/n, initial h/R).
- Which face is recto and which verso is undeterminable; my "face 1 / face 2" follows image order only. That the two images are two faces of one scrap is inferred from the mirrored outline.
- Face 2 line 4 and the top of face 1 are cut by tears; the tissue covers nothing written as far as I can see, but writing under the opaque tissue edge cannot be excluded.
- A wider view is not available (this is the whole scrap); sibling scraps from the same leaf would be needed for any checkable span.
- I did nothing beyond the rules: opened only PROMPT.md and the four image files of this packet.
